Class ECMWFAction

java.lang.Object
org.apache.struts.action.Action
ecmwf.ecpds.master.plugin.http.controller.ECMWFAction
Direct Known Subclasses:
InteractiveLoginAction, LoginAction, LogoutAction, PDSAction
public abstract class ECMWFAction extends org.apache.struts.action.Action
This is intended to an abstract base class for all Actions, handling exceptions and providing utility methods to get user information.
Author:
Daniel Varela Santoalla

    • processParameterEnsuringBasePath

      protected Collection processParameterEnsuringBasePath(javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request, String parameter, String actionPath) throws ECMWFException

      struts-config.xml mappings path match only uses the part of the path with is AFTER the web.xml servlet mapping. This way, if we have multiple Apache and Tomcat servlets mapping pointing to the ActionServlet, struts is not able to make a difference between them and will execute the same Actions independently of the Apache/Tomcat mod_jk/web.xml mappings triggered.

      We don't want this because since our Access Control is based on URLs, we'd have to protect all possible combinations of Apache+Tomcat/Struts mappings. So this method will user the "parameter" attribute of "action" to ensure that the Apache+Tomcat mapping is the only one we want. This solution is not perfect because reverse mappings from invalid input: '<'html:form> tags won't work (which servlet mapping to use?) but it will do till Struts 1.2, where the Modules feature should provide for this.

      Parameters:
      request - The HTTP request
      parameter - The Apache+Tomcat mapping WE KNOW (via "parameter") that is the only one which can access this Action. After it, comma separated, path parameters.
      actionPath - The path of the action mapped.
      Returns:
      A Collection will all path parameters or NULL if none.
      Throws:
      ECMWFException
